source: Karnataka NMMS SAT 2019 question paper, NMMS-SAT-P2 (K-8) (pyq/ka-2019-20-sat.pdf), English version. The paper numbers its options 1) to 4); here they are A) to D). The paper has no answer key.

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The velocity of a car is 18 m s⁻¹. Its velocity in km h⁻¹ is :

solution.concept: 8.3 Speed: 1 m/s = 3.6 km/h

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The amplitude of a sound wave determines its :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Sound: the amplitude of a vibration decides how loud the sound is
steps: Amplitude is how far the vibrating object moves from its rest position
A larger amplitude gives a louder sound, so amplitude decides the volume
Frequency decides the pitch; the period and the wavelength go with the frequency, not the amplitude

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The natural tendency of objects to resist a change in their state is :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Force, Motion and Energy: inertia is the tendency of a body to stay at rest or in uniform motion
steps: An object keeps its state of rest or motion unless a force acts on it
This tendency to resist a change of state is called inertia
Mass is the measure of inertia, but the tendency itself is inertia

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The potential energy of an object of mass 2 kg at a height of 15 m is :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Force, Motion and Energy: potential energy = m × g × h
steps: m = 2 kg, g = 9.8 m/s², h = 15 m

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: A particle moves 3 m north, then 4 m east and finally 6 m south from its initial point. Then its total displacement is :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Force, Motion and Energy: displacement is the straight-line distance from the start to the end point
steps: 3 m north and then 6 m south leaves the particle 3 m south of the start
It is also 4 m east, so the start, the end and the corner make a right triangle
Displacement = √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5 m

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: One hertz is equal to :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Sound: frequency is the number of vibrations per second, measured in hertz (Hz)
steps: 1 Hz = 1 vibration per second
1 minute = 60 seconds, so 1 Hz = 60 vibrations per minute

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: Two persons pull a box in the same direction with 15 N and 25 N. If the net displacement of the box is 20 m, then the work done is :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Force, Motion and Energy: work = force × displacement; forces in the same direction add up
steps: Net force = 15 N + 25 N = 40 N
Work = 40 N × 20 m = 800 J

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: According to Newton’s third law of motion, action and reaction act on :

options.B: The same object in the same direction
options.C: The same object in opposite directions
options.D: Different objects in the same direction

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Force, Motion and Energy: Newton’s third law: action and reaction are equal and opposite
steps: Action and reaction always act on two different objects
They are equal in size and opposite in direction

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The average velocity of a particle moving in a straight line with initial velocity ‘u’ and constant acceleration ‘a’ in ‘t’ seconds is :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Force, Motion and Energy: with constant acceleration, average velocity = (initial + final velocity) ÷ 2
steps: Final velocity v = u + at
Average velocity = (u + u + at) ÷ 2 = u + at/2

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The velocity of sound in vacuum is :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Sound: sound needs a medium (solid, liquid or gas) to travel
steps: A vacuum has no particles to pass the vibrations on
So sound cannot travel in a vacuum: its speed there is 0 m/s

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The temperature range of a clinical thermometer is :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Heat and Temperature: a clinical thermometer only needs to cover human body temperatures
steps: Normal body temperature is about 37 °C
A person’s temperature stays between about 35 °C and 42 °C, so that is the scale

questions.subject: physics
questions.prompt: The number of images formed when the angle between two plane mirrors is 72° :

solution.concept: 11.8.2 Kaleidoscope: mirrors at an angle give many images by repeated reflection
steps: Number of images = 360° ÷ (angle between the mirrors) − 1

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: The model that explains “the energy of an electron remains constant so long as it revolves in its own shell” is :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Structure of the Atom: Bohr’s model: electrons move in fixed shells (orbits) without losing energy
steps: Bohr said an electron in its own shell neither gains nor loses energy
Rutherford’s model could not explain this; Thomson’s had no shells at all

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: If the gas in a discharge tube is heavier, then the deflection of the anode rays is :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Structure of the Atom: anode rays are positive ions of the gas in the tube; heavier particles are deflected less
steps: The anode rays are made of the gas’s own positive ions
A heavier gas gives heavier ions, which turn least in an electric or magnetic field

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: The percentage by mass of nitrogen in HNO₃ is :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Structure of the Atom: % of an element = its mass in one molecule ÷ molecular mass × 100

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: In any given sample of chlorine, the ratio of the atomic masses of its two isotopes is :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Structure of the Atom: isotopes of an element have different masses; chlorine is a mixture of chlorine-35 and chlorine-37
steps: In any sample of chlorine, about 3 atoms in 4 are chlorine-35 and 1 in 4 is chlorine-37: a ratio of 3 : 1
That is why chlorine’s average atomic mass is 35.5
Note: the masses themselves are 35 : 37; the paper means the ratio in which the two isotopes occur

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: The instrument used to find atomic mass accurately is :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Structure of the Atom: atomic masses are measured accurately with a mass spectroscope (mass spectrometer)
steps: A mass spectroscope separates atoms by their mass and measures it
An optical spectroscope studies light, and a microscope only magnifies

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: The decomposition of limestone into quick lime is :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Chemical Reactions: a reaction that takes in heat is endothermic
steps: Limestone (CaCO₃) breaks into quicklime (CaO) and CO₂ only when heated strongly
It keeps taking in heat, so the reaction is endothermic

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: The balanced chemical equation among the following is :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Chemical Reactions: a balanced equation uses correct formulae and has the same number of each atom on both sides
steps: Mercury oxide is HgO and oxygen gas is O₂
2HgO → 2Hg + O₂: 2 Hg and 2 O on each side ✓
A and C use wrong formulae (HgO₂, Hg₂); D writes oxygen gas as O

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: The chemical name of Epsom salt is :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Chemical Reactions: common names of salts
steps: Epsom salt is magnesium sulphate (MgSO₄ · 7H₂O)
Sodium sulphate is Glauber’s salt; calcium sulphate is gypsum

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: Match the following :

options.A: A - b, B - d, C - a, D - c
options.B: A - c, B - a, C - d, D - b
options.C: A - d, B - c, C - b, D - a
options.D: A - c, B - d, C - b, D - a

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Structure of the Atom: the most electrons each subshell holds: s 2, p 6, d 10, f 14

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: The chemical compound used to prevent the growth of bacteria and fungi is :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Food Preservation: chemical preservatives stop the growth of microbes
steps: Sulphur dioxide (SO₂, used as its sulphite salts) is a common chemical preservative
MgO₂, CaCO₃ and CaO are not used to preserve food

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.prompt: The gas flushed into packets of chips to prevent rancidity is :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Food Preservation: rancidity is the oxidation of fats and oils by the oxygen in air
steps: Chips packets are filled with nitrogen, an unreactive gas, in place of air
With no oxygen, the oil in the chips does not turn rancid

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: A biological molecule has to move out of the mitochondrial matrix to the cytoplasm to enter other organelles. The number of membranes it has to move across :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – The Cell: a mitochondrion has two membranes, an outer and an inner one
steps: The matrix is the space inside the inner membrane
To reach the cytoplasm a molecule crosses the inner and then the outer membrane: two membranes

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: The following is an example of a parasitic food chain :

solution.concept: 12.4 Parasitism: a parasite lives on a host and feeds on it
steps: In A, lice live on the birds and feed on them: the chain passes from a host to its parasite
B starts from dead matter (a detritus chain); C and D are chains of eating (predation)

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: The correct matching of minerals and their functions :

options.A: A - iii, B - i, C - ii, D - iv
options.B: A - iv, B - ii, C - i, D - iii
options.C: A - ii, B - iv, C - iii, D - i
options.D: A - i, B - iii, C - iv, D - ii

solution.concept: 3.4.2 Minerals in food: lack of iodine causes goitre and lack of iron causes anaemia
steps: Iodine prevents goitre (B – iv); iron in the blood carries oxygen (C – iii)
Sodium helps control blood pressure (A – ii), and zinc takes the one left, reducing cholesterol deposits (D – i)

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Yeast is added to grape juice, which is kept for a long time to make wine. This process is :

solution.concept: 2.4.2 Yeast ferments sugar into alcohol and carbon dioxide
steps: In a closed vessel the yeast has little oxygen
Breaking down sugar without oxygen (fermentation) is anaerobic respiration

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: The correct pair of parasites among the following :

solution.concept: 12.4 Parasitism: Cuscuta and tapeworms are parasites
steps: Cuscuta lives on other plants and tapeworms live in the intestines: both feed on a host
Nepenthes traps insects; a mushroom feeds on dead matter; an earthworm lives freely in soil

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: The cell membrane is described as a semipermeable membrane because :

options.A: It helps to maintain the shape of the cell
options.B: It provides an internal framework to the cell
options.C: It plays an important role in the synthesis of proteins
options.D: It controls the movement of selected substances in and out of the cell

solution.concept: 2.1 Cell membrane: a porous boundary that controls what enters and leaves the cell
steps: It lets some substances through and stops others, so it is called semipermeable
Shape and framework come from other parts (the cell wall in plants)

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: The true statement about fungi :

options.B: Their cell wall is composed of cellulose

solution.concept: 2.3 Fungi: moulds like Rhizopus, Aspergillus and Penicillium grow from spores
steps: Fungi reproduce by spores ✓
Fungi have a nucleus (bacteria are the prokaryotes), their cell wall is not cellulose, and only some fungi are parasites

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: In the given diagram of Amoeba, the parts labelled A, B and C respectively are :

options.A: Pseudopodia, Food vacuole and Contractile vacuole
options.C: Contractile vacuole, Food vacuole and Nucleus

solution.concept: 2.3 Amoeba: a single cell that moves with pseudopodia (false feet)
steps: A: a finger-like outgrowth of the cell is a pseudopodium
B: the large round body with threads inside is the nucleus
C: the small body with food inside is a food vacuole

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Unused carbohydrates in the body are stored as :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Nutrition, Respiration and Excretion in Animals: the body stores extra food as fat
steps: Carbohydrates not used for energy are turned into fat and stored
Proteins, vitamins and minerals are not stores of unused carbohydrate

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: In a cockroach, carbon dioxide diffuses out of the body through the :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – Nutrition, Respiration and Excretion in Animals: insects breathe through spiracles that open into air tubes (tracheae)
steps: Gases move between the body and the air through small openings on the sides of the body, the spiracles
Tracheae and tracheoles are the tubes inside; alveoli are found in human lungs

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Chlamydomonas responds to light. This is due to the presence of :

solution.concept: Old syllabus – The Cell: Chlamydomonas has a light-sensitive eyespot, the stigma
steps: The red eyespot (stigma) senses light, and the cell swims towards it
Pyrenoids store starch; contractile vacuoles remove water

questions.subject: biology
questions.prompt: Viruses insert their genetic material into the host cell :

solution.concept: 2.3 Viruses reproduce only inside the cells of a host
steps: A virus puts its genetic material into a host cell so that the cell makes new viruses
So the purpose is to reproduce

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: The perimeter of an equilateral triangle is 45 cm. The length of each side is :

solution.concept: 7.1 & 7.2 Classifying triangles by sides: an equilateral triangle has three equal sides
steps: Perimeter = side + side + side = 3 × side
3 × side = 45 cm, so side = 45 ÷ 3 = 15 cm

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: In the figure, if ∆KLM ≅ ∆PQM, then the value of ‘x’ is :

solution.concept: 1.2 Congruence of triangles: corresponding parts of congruent triangles are equal
steps: ∆KLM ≅ ∆PQM, so the matching sides KM and PM are equal
4x² + 2x = 4x² + 6
Take 4x² from both sides: 2x = 6, so x = 3

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: In the figure, AB ∥ CD. The measure of ∠AEC is :

solution.concept: 5.5–5.8 Parallel lines and a transversal: co-interior angles add up to 180°
steps: Draw a line through E parallel to AB (and so to CD). It splits ∠AEC into two parts
Upper part: 180° − 109° = 71° (co-interior with ∠BAE)
Lower part: 180° − 115° = 65° (co-interior with ∠DCE)

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: The median of the scores 40, 52, 34, 47, 31, 35, 48, 41, 44, 38 is :

solution.concept: 5.2 Representative values: the median is the middle value once the data is in order
steps: There are 10 scores (even), so the median is the mean of the 5th and 6th

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: If √(a/b) = (b/a)¹⁻³ˣ, then the value of ‘x’ is :

solution.concept: 2.3 Negative exponents and laws of exponents: √n = n^(1/2) and (a/b)⁻ᵐ = (b/a)ᵐ
steps: So (b/a)^(−1/2) = (b/a)^(1 − 3x): the bases are the same, so the exponents are equal

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: The ratio of the cost price to the selling price is 5 : 7. The profit percent is :

solution.concept: 8.3 Profit and loss: profit % is always worked out on the cost price
steps: Take CP = 5 parts and SP = 7 parts
Profit = 7 − 5 = 2 parts

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: In the figure, ∠AOB and ∠DEF are :

solution.concept: 5.1 Angle pairs: two angles that add up to 180° are supplementary
steps: ∠AOB = 120° and ∠DEF = 60°
120° + 60° = 180°, so they are supplementary
They are not adjacent or vertically opposite: they are at different points

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: A 3 × 3 magic square is made using the even numbers from 2 to 18. The magic sum is :

solution.concept: 6.3 Magic squares: the 3 rows share the total equally, so magic sum = total ÷ 3
steps: The numbers are 2, 4, 6, …, 18 (nine numbers)
Magic sum = 90 ÷ 3 = 30

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: The numbers of boys and girls in a class are in the ratio 7 : 5. There are 8 more boys than girls. The total number of students in the class is :

solution.concept: 7.1–7.3 Ratios: write each quantity as a number of equal parts
steps: Boys = 7 parts, girls = 5 parts
7 − 5 = 2 parts = 8 students, so 1 part = 4
Total = 12 parts = 12 × 4 = 48

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: A seven-digit number is written as 35A2479, where ‘A’ is a digit. The number is exactly divisible by 11. The value of ‘A’ is :

solution.concept: 5.2 Divisibility by 11: the alternating sum of the digits (from the units digit) must be 0 or a multiple of 11
steps: Digits from the right: 9, 7, 4, 2, A, 5, 3
Alternating sum = 9 − 7 + 4 − 2 + A − 5 + 3 = A + 2
A + 2 must be 0 or 11, so A = 9

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: A person sold a table for ₹2250 and gained one-ninth of its cost price. The cost price of the table is :

solution.concept: 8.3 Profit and loss: SP = CP + profit, and the profit is a fraction of the CP
steps: Profit = CP/9, so SP = CP + CP/9 = 10/9 × CP

questions.prompt: If √(1 + 27/169) = 1 + m/13, then the value of ‘m’ is :

solution.concept: 1.1 Square roots of fractions: √(a/b) = √a / √b
6.2 Standard identity: a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: One third of a number, when added to 1, gives 5. The number is :

solution.concept: 7.2 Solving equations by balancing and transposition
steps: Let the number be x: x/3 + 1 = 5

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: If a/b = 2 and c/b = 3, then the value of (a + b)/(b + c) is :

solution.concept: 7.1–7.3 Ratios: write every quantity in terms of one of them
steps: a/b = 2, so a = 2b; c/b = 3, so c = 3b

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: In the figure, the value of ‘x’ is :

solution.concept: 7.3 Exterior angle property: an exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles
steps: Extend BD to meet AC at E
In ∆ABE, exterior ∠DEC = ∠A + ∠ABE = 60° + 20° = 80°
In ∆DEC, exterior x = ∠DEC + ∠C = 80° + 40° = 120°
Shortcut: in such an arrowhead, x = 60° + 20° + 40°

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: In the figure, AB ∥ CE and CD ∥ EF. The value of ‘x’ is :

solution.concept: 5.5–5.8 Parallel lines: corresponding angles are equal and co-interior angles add up to 180°
steps: AB ∥ CE with transversal AD: ∠ECD = ∠BAC = 75° (corresponding angles)
CD ∥ EF with transversal CE: x + ∠ECD = 180° (co-interior angles)

questions.prompt: Taking only the positive roots, the value of √(41 − √(21 + √(19 − √9))) is :

solution.concept: 1.1 Square roots: work from the innermost root outwards

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: The factors of (a² + b² − c² − 2ab) are :

solution.concept: 6.2 Standard identities: a² − 2ab + b² = (a − b)² and x² − y² = (x + y)(x − y)
steps: a² + b² − 2ab − c² = (a − b)² − c²
= (a − b − c)(a − b + c)

questions.subject: maths
questions.prompt: If x² + 1/x² = 102, then the value of x − 1/x is (take only the positive root) :

solution.concept: 6.2 Standard identity: (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b²
